problems.title: Stable sets and low query dispersion do not imply zero information
problems.source_location: Remark 1, current arXiv v2 PDF p.6; Appendix G.10, p.38
claim: The paper calls IP and set-size-stability stopping criteria equivalent and uses low dispersion of candidate postquery entropies as a practical stopping diagnostic.
analysis: Let \(Y=X\) be a bit with \(P(Y=0)=0.9\), and let an uninformative predictor always return \((0.95,0.05)\), producing singleton set \(\{0\}\). At \(\alpha=0.1,N=100\), coverage \(0.9\) lies within the stated two-sided range. A query revealing Y leaves that predictor’s set size unchanged but gains \(h_b(0.1)\approx0.468996\) bits. Separately, for a fair bit, candidate queries Y and its complement both have zero postquery entropy and zero dispersion, while each gains one bit.
result: Neither stable conformal-set size nor equal candidate entropy scores certifies informational sufficiency. The paper explicitly leaves adaptive error control open, and this finding does not claim poor empirical stopping performance.
repair: Describe the stopping tests as heuristics. An exact no-information condition compares current entropy with the answer-weighted expected postquery entropy; a finite-sample stopping guarantee needs additional estimation control.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local stopping-interpretation overstatement, not a refutation of the valid entropy upper bound or an established empirical performance failure.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Released query score differs from log mean set size
problems.source_location: Section 3.2, Eqs.(9)–(11), PDF p.5; src/20q/20q_conformal_closed_binary.py, lines 190–203
claim: The displayed C-IP rule minimizes log expected prediction-set size; the release instead computes a conditional mean-log Fano-style score and uses estimation batch size where calibration size belongs.
analysis: With four included-label samples and set sizes \(A=(1,1,1,9)\), \(B=(2,2,2,2)\), the displayed mean-size objective prefers B because \(\log_2 3>\log_2 2\). The release at \(\alpha=0.1,n=4\) gives \(h_b(0.1)+1.1\operatorname{mean}\log_2 S\), with scores approximately \(1.340725\) and \(1.568996\), preferring A. These sets are realizable by normalized thresholded probability vectors. The alternate population Fano bound is legitimate; it simply differs from the displayed method. The coefficient uses \(n=4\) instead of calibration \(N=100\).
result: The implementation can reverse query rankings relative to the stated surrogate. Its alternative bound is not itself a false information-theoretic theorem, and the resulting change in benchmark query traces is not measured.
repair: Implement log of mean size with the stated calibration parameter, or explicitly document the different conditional-log objective and justify its estimator, including empty groups.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a release/method correspondence discrepancy; the mathematical source bound remains valid and benchmark effects are unmeasured.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Prior answer weights do not estimate the history-conditional objective
problems.source_location: Eq.(2), PDF p.3; C-IP rule p.6; src/20q/20q_entropy_closed_binary.py, sample_data and estimate_entropy
claim: The desired next-answer expectation is conditional on the observed history, but the release samples unconditional labels and then appends their answers to that history.
analysis: Let Y be uniform on \(20\) labels and history restrict it to \(H=\{0,1,2,3,4,5\}\). Query A is true for label zero or labels at least six; query B is true for \[\{0,1,2,6,7,8,9,10,11,12\}\]. Both answers remain possible after history. Exact posterior entropies give conditional scores \(H_A=(5/6)\log_2 5\approx1.93494\), \(H_B=\log_2 3\approx1.58496\), so B is preferred. Prior weights instead give \(\widetilde H_A=(5/20)\log_2 5\approx0.580482\) and the same B score, selecting A. Correct inner posteriors cannot fix incorrect outer answer probabilities.
result: The released IP expectation can rank the less informative query first even with an oracle posterior. The first query and history-independent answers are valid special cases; the exact numeric example is not claimed to characterize the full C-IP inclusion/exclusion score.
repair: Sample from the history-conditional law or apply justified likelihood importance weights. General free-text histories require an explicitly validated conditional sampler.
problems.impact_rationale: This identifies a bounded implemented-estimator mismatch, rather than a false information identity or measured benchmark reversal.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Calibration quantile lacks the general finite-sample adjustment
claim: The release uses the higher empirical quantile at \(1-\alpha\), whose calibration rank differs from the split-conformal finite-sample rank.
analysis: For \(N=21,\alpha=0.1\), the code rank is \(\lceil20(0.9)\rceil+1=19\), while the required rank is \(\lceil22(0.9)\rceil=20\). Permute \(22\) distinct valid scores \(s_j=-j/23\), represented by two-label probabilities \((-s_j,1+s_j)\) with true label zero. Exchangeability makes the held-out rank uniform, so the release covers \(19/22<0.9\), while the corrected rank covers \(20/22\). For \(N=50,\alpha=0.01\), the required unavailable rank needs an infinite threshold rather than the largest observed score. The reported \(N=100,200\) settings on the inspected level grid happen to satisfy the rank inequality.
result: The quantile is not generally valid under the advertised exchangeable-score domain. This arithmetic defect does not explain every reported undercoverage curve or resolve adaptive-history exchangeability.
repair: Use rank \(\lceil(N+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil\), returning an infinite threshold if it exceeds N, and include scores non-strictly at the threshold.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a general release calibration-boundary defect with explicit favorable controls at the paper’s reported calibration sizes.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

impact_rationale: Minor: local stopping and implemented-estimator/calibration discrepancies are supported, while the central entropy upper bound and untested empirical gains are not disproved.
